title: Webb telescope finds changing rings on Chariklo

slides.headline: Webb telescope finds changing rings on Chariklo
slides.subtitle: The inner ring is getting more opaque

slides.explanation: Chariklo is a small object orbiting between Saturn and Uranus. It is tiny compared to major planets but complex enough to hold its own ring system.

slides.headline: Rings around small bodies evolve much faster than expected
slides.explanation: Astronomers once thought these rings were relatively static. Now we see one ring darkening while the other fades over just a few years.
This finding is confirmed by four independent science outlets, including Space.com and New Scientist. When multiple experts agree on the data, we can be confident in the discovery.

caption:
The James Webb Space Telescope is changing how we view the solar system.

By observing Chariklo, a small object tucked between Saturn and Uranus, researchers spotted something unexpected.

Over the course of just a few years, the rings surrounding this object have shifted in opacity. The inner ring has become more opaque, while the outer one has grown less so.

This suggests that the rings on smaller celestial bodies are far more dynamic than we previously assumed. It challenges the idea that these systems are stagnant or slow to change.

story.title: James Webb reveals Chariklo’s mysterious rings are changing faster than expected
story.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has revealed surprising changes in the rings around Chariklo, a small object orbiting between Saturn and Uranus. Over just a few years, its inner ring became more opaque while its outer ring became less opaque. The results suggest that rings around small Solar System bodies may be much more dynamic than scientists previously believed. What is causing the changes remains a mystery.
